passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: (dollars in millions, except per share, per ounce and per pound amounts) The following Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Consolidated Financial Condition and Results of Operations (“MD&A”) provides information that management believes is relevant to an assessment and understanding of the consolidated financial condition and results of operations of Newmont Corporation, a Delaware corporation, and its subsidiaries (collectively, “Newmont,” the “Company,” “our” and “we”). We use certain non-GAAP financial measures in our MD&A. For a detailed description of each of the non-GAAP measures used in this MD&A, please refer to the discussion under Non-GAAP Financial Measures. This item should be read in conjunction with our Consolidated Financial Statements and the notes thereto included in this annual report. The following MD&A generally discusses our consolidated financial condition and results of operations for 2025 and 2024 and year-to-year comparisons between 2025 and 2024. Discussions of our consolidated financial condition and results of operations for 2023 and year-to-year comparisons between 2024 and 2023 are included in Item 7, Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Consolidated Financial Condition and Results of Operations, of the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K , filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on February 21, 2025. Overview Newmont is the world’s leading gold company and is the only gold company included in the S&P 500 Index and the Fortune 500 list of companies. We have been included in the Dow Jones Sustainability Index-World since 2007 and have adopted the World Gold Council’s Conflict-Free Gold Policy. Since 2015, Newmont has been ranked as the mining and metal sector’s top gold miner by the S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment. Newmont has been ranked the top miner in 3BL Media’s 100 Best Corporate Citizens list which ranks the 1,000 largest publicly traded U.S. companies on ESG transparency and performance since 2020. We are primarily engaged in the exploration for and acquisition of gold properties, some of which may contain copper, silver, lead, zinc or other metals. We have significant operations and/or assets in the United States, Papua New Guinea, Australia, Ghana, Suriname, Argentina, Dominican Republic, Chile, Peru, Ecuador, Mexico, and Canada. Our goal is to create value and improve lives through sustainable and responsible mining. Refer to the Consolidated Financial Results, Results of Consolidated Operations, Liquidity and Capital Resources and Non-GAAP Financial Measures for information about the continued impacts from inflationary pressures, effects of certain countermeasures taken by central banks, and supply chain disruptions, with particular consideration on the outlook for increased costs specific to labor, materials, consumables and fuel and energy on operations, as well as impacts on the timing and cost of capital expenditures and the risk of potential impairment to certain assets. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: (dollars in millions, except per share, per ounce and per pound amounts) Our business activities are subject to significant risks, including those described below. You should carefully consider these risks. If any of the described risks actually occurs, our business, financial position and results of operations could be materially adversely affected. Such risks are not the only ones we face and additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also affect our business. This report contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results could differ materially from those anticipated in the forward-looking statements as a result of a number of factors, including the risks described below. Refer to “Forward-Looking Statements.” Risks Related to Our Operations and Business A substantial or extended decline in gold, copper, silver, lead or zinc prices would have a material adverse effect on us. Our business is dependent on the prices of gold, copper, silver, lead and zinc, which fluctuate on a daily basis and are affected by numerous factors beyond our control. Factors tending to influence prices include: • Gold sales, purchases or leasing by governments and central banks; • Speculative short positions taken by significant investors or traders in gold, copper, silver, lead, zinc or other metals; • The relative strength of the U.S. dollar; • The monetary policies employed by the world’s major Central Banks; • The fiscal policies employed by the world’s major industrialized economies; • Expectations of the future rate of inflation; • Interest rates; • Recession or reduced economic activity in the United States, Australia, China, India and other industrialized or developing countries; • Decreased industrial, jewelry, base metal or investment demand; • Increased import and export taxes; • Increased supply from production, disinvestment and scrap; • Forward sales by producers in hedging or similar transactions; • Availability of cheaper substitute materials; and • Changing investor or consumer sentiment, including in connection with transition to a low-carbon economy, investor interest in crypto currencies and other investment alternatives and other factors. Average gold prices for 2025 were $3,432 per ounce (2024: $2,386; 2023: $1,941), average copper prices for 2025 were $4.51 per pound (2024: $4.15; 2023: $3.85), average silver prices for 2025 were $40.03 per ounce (2024: $28.27; 2023: $23.35), average lead prices for 2025 were $0.89 per pound (2024: $0.94; 2023: $0.97), and average zinc prices for 2025 were $1.30 per pound (2024: $1.26; 2023: $1.20). Prices are obtained from the London Bullion Market Association for gold and silver and the London Metal Exchange for copper, lead and zinc. Any decline in our realized prices adversely impacts our revenues, net income and operating cash flows, particularly in light of our strategy of not engaging in hedging transactions with respect to sales of gold, copper, silver, lead or zinc. credit_strengths.text: Newmont's operating cash flow covers capital spending and distributions with room to spare, reflecting the cash-generative nature of its global gold portfolio. Free cash flow exceeds total debt, a rare feat among peers, and supports the company's investment-grade profile. This internally funded model reduces reliance on external financing and provides a buffer against commodity price swings.

The balance sheet carries more cash than debt, producing negative net leverage and a net cash position. This liquidity cushion, combined with a current ratio above the sector median, underscores strong short-term solvency. Management's conservative capital structure provides flexibility to fund growth or return capital without stressing credit metrics.

key_risks.text: Newmont's results are highly sensitive to gold, copper, and other metal prices, which are volatile and beyond management's control. The company does not hedge its sales, so a sustained price decline would directly pressure revenue and operating cash flow. This commodity price exposure is the dominant risk factor disclosed in the filing.

Debt maturities are heavily weighted to later years, with a large portion due after year five. While near-term maturities are minimal, the company will need to refinance or repay these notes, potentially at higher rates. The revolving credit facility remains undrawn, providing a backstop, but reliance on capital markets for future refinancing is a structural consideration.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is exceptionally high, with operating income dwarfing interest expense. This provides a substantial cushion against earnings volatility. Even if metal prices fell sharply, the company's ability to service its debt from operating profits would remain robust, as reflected in the minimal indicative financial risk profile.

Free cash flow to debt exceeds one times, indicating that a single year's free cash flow could theoretically repay all debt. This strong cash conversion, supported by high operating margins, suggests debt servicing is comfortably within the company's capacity. The undrawn revolver further enhances liquidity and refinancing flexibility.

overall_credit_view.text: Newmont exhibits a minimal credit risk profile, characterized by net cash, high profitability, and strong cash flow generation. Leverage is far below sector medians, and coverage ratios are exceptional. The company's scale and diversified operations support a stable outlook, though commodity price exposure remains the primary credit driver.

Shareholder distributions absorb a significant portion of free cash flow, but the remaining buffer is ample. With no near-term maturities and substantial cash, refinancing risk is low. We view the credit as well-positioned to withstand cyclical downturns, though a prolonged price slump could pressure cash flows and shareholder return capacity.

credit_strengths.text: 紐蒙特嘅營運現金流足以覆蓋資本開支同分派，仲有餘裕，反映其全球黃金組合嘅現金生成能力。自由現金流超過總債務，喺同業中屬罕見，並支持公司嘅投資級別狀況。呢個內部融資模式減少對外部融資嘅依賴，並為商品價格波動提供緩衝。
資產負債表持有嘅現金多過債務，產生負淨槓桿同淨現金狀況。呢個流動性緩衝，加上流動比率高於行業中位數，突顯強勁嘅短期償付能力。管理層嘅保守資本結構提供靈活性，可以為增長提供資金或返還資本，而唔會對信貸指標造成壓力。

key_risks.text: 紐蒙特嘅業績對黃金、銅及其他金屬價格高度敏感，呢啲價格波動且超出管理層控制。公司並無對沖其銷售，因此價格持續下跌會直接對收入同營運現金流構成壓力。呢個商品價格風險敞口係申報文件中披露嘅主要風險因素。
債務到期日嚴重集中喺較後年份，其中一大部分喺五年後到期。雖然近期到期債務極少，但公司將需要為呢啲票據再融資或償還，可能喺更高利率下進行。循環信貸額度仍未提取，提供咗後備支持，但未來再融資依賴資本市場係一個結構性考慮因素。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率極高，營運收入遠超利息開支。呢個為盈利波動提供咗重大緩衝。即使金屬價格大幅下跌，公司從營運利潤償還債務嘅能力仍會保持穩健，正如最低指示性財務風險狀況所反映。
自由現金流對債務比率超過一倍，表明單一年度嘅自由現金流理論上可以償還所有債務。呢個強勁嘅現金轉換，得到高營運利潤率支持，表明債務償還完全喺公司能力範圍內。未提取嘅循環信貸進一步增強流動性同再融資靈活性。

overall_credit_view.text: 紐蒙特展現最低信貸風險狀況，其特點係淨現金、高盈利能力同強勁現金流生成。槓桿遠低於行業中位數，而覆蓋比率異常出色。公司嘅規模同多元化業務支持穩定展望，儘管商品價格風險敞口仍然係主要信貸驅動因素。
股東分派吸收咗自由現金流嘅重要部分，但剩餘緩衝充足。由於並無近期到期債務同大量現金，再融資風險低。我們認為該信貸狀況良好，能夠抵禦週期性低迷，儘管價格長期低迷可能會對現金流同股東回報能力構成壓力。
